title: Polynomial-Time Block XOR Test
statement: Let $V$ be a language of finite bit strings whose Boolean membership indicator, output as a one-bit word, is polynomial-time computable. For any $a,k,a',k'\in\mathbb{N}$, the following function is polynomial-time computable: on input $w$, parse its first component as a pair to obtain $x$ (using the empty word if parsing fails), and let $y$ be the second component of $w$ (again using the empty word if parsing fails). For each of the first $a'(|x|+1)^{k'}$ blocks of length $a(|x|+1)^k$ in the parsed second component of the inner pair, take the bitwise XOR with the corresponding initial segment of $y$, truncating to the shorter word; the output is true exactly when at least one resulting word, paired with $x$, belongs to $V$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language of finite bit strings
The one-bit membership indicator of $V$ is polynomial-time computable
